sections.heading: Pumping at each step
sections.body_md: As electrons move along the chain, three of the complexes act as pumps. Each uses a portion of the released energy to push protons from the inner space of the mitochondrion out across the inner membrane.

sections.heading: Storing energy as a gradient
sections.body_md: Because protons are pushed to one side faster than they leak back, they pile up. The result is both a concentration difference and a charge difference across the membrane, and together these store energy the cell can later tap.

key_points: Three complexes pump protons as electrons pass.
The build-up stores energy as a concentration and charge difference.
